solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Novelist Roald's 23as narrated by Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner names the reverend who swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words said here trade their first sounds

parts.note: Roald Dahl, the children's author, so Roald's is Dahl's
23 across is LAYER, and layers are hens, here called chickens

explanation.surface: A literary aside about some novelist's account of Roald Dahl's hens.
explanation.walkthrough: '23as' means the answer to 23 Across made plural: layers, or laying hens. Dahl's chickens, with the opening sounds swapped by Spooner, gives the Victorian novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Oliver Twist and Bleak House is among the most famous of all English novelists.

clue.text: Boca Juniors holding player from Baton Rouge

indicators.note: the Argentine club's name holds the answer within its letters, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A football club, Boca Juniors, is said to have signed a player from Louisiana.
explanation.walkthrough: Boca Juniors is a Buenos Aires football club, so 'player' seems to mean a footballer; it is a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Cajun music is the folk style of French-descended Louisiana, so a Cajun from around Baton Rouge could be a musician playing it.

clue.text: Sold 22 off for garrison town

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad or wrong, telling us the letters are spoiled into a new arrangement

parts.note: the answer to 22 Down is EARTH

explanation.surface: Land being sold off near a garrison town.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLD with EARTH, the answer to 22 Down, is rearranged ('off'). Aldershot in Hampshire is the traditional home of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hampshire town has been the British Army's main base since the 1850s, a classic military garrison.

clue.text: 11 people reported oversight

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the clue gives a word heard rather than read

parts.note: 11 Across is NORSE; the Lapps are a people of Norway's far north

explanation.surface: A report blames a lapse on people from Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: The 11 refers to the answer at 11 Across (NORSE). The Sami of northern Scandinavia were long called Lapps, which is said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or failure of attention, much as an oversight is a mistake made by not noticing.

clue.text: Pain at its worst, therefore lie down

parts.note: so can mean therefore, as in 'so it follows'
to rest is to lie down

explanation.surface: Advice that when pain is at its worst you should lie down.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of sore, describing pain at its most intense, the most painful it gets.

clue.text: Press college boy for battleship

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A college boy being pressed into service on a battleship.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironclad was a nineteenth-century warship armoured with iron plates, the forerunner of the modern battleship.

clue.text: Con government, nothing special, treated by the media with these?

definitions.text: treated by the media with these?

parts.note: to kid someone is to con or fool them
love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A jibe that the Conservative government, unremarkable as it is, gets gentle treatment from the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' looks like shorthand for Conservative, but it means swindle. To handle someone with kid gloves is to treat them very gently.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloves of soft kid leather give the idiom for handling someone with great tact and delicacy, as the media are said to do here.

clue.text: Southern African American stuck between US coastal cities

indicators.note: something stuck between two others sits in the middle of them

parts.note: NY is New York on the east coast and LA is Los Angeles on the west

explanation.surface: An American from the south stuck between New York and Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Southern African American' reads as one phrase about a person; the definition stops at 'African'.
explanation.definitionFit: This spiral-horned antelope is native to south-eastern Africa, so it is a southern African animal.

clue.text: Placed emphasis on turnover of sweets

indicators.note: turning a word over makes it read backwards

parts.note: desserts are sweets in the sense of puddings

explanation.surface: Someone who placed emphasis on a turnover among the puddings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' tempts as a pastry among the sweets; it signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a word or point is to give it emphasis, so stressed is the past tense for placed emphasis on.

clue.text: PhD returned during day to the French fort city

indicators.note: during means within the span of the day, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: jour is the French word for day

indicators.note: returned means the doctorate's letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: A doctoral graduate going back to a fortified city on a French day trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Jodhpur in Rajasthan is dominated by the Mehrangarh Fort, one of India's great fortified cities.

clue.text: Retired sailor using LSD a lot

indicators.note: using the letters given, as a drug user uses, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A pensioned-off seaman taking a lot of acid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Using' reads as drug taking with LSD but tells us to rearrange L, S, D, A, L, O, T.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is a veteran seaman with long experience, one who may well have retired from the sea.

clue.text: Norwegian King garlanded with bouquet

indicators.note: a thing garlanded is wrapped round, so the second word surrounds the first

parts.note: a wine's bouquet is its nose
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A Norwegian king crowned with a wreath of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' suggests flowers to fit 'garlanded', but it is the aroma of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse describes the language and people of ancient Scandinavia, including Norway.

clue.text: Skive off with Alec and claim this?

definitions.text: Skive off with Alec and claim this?

indicators.note: off suggests something gone awry, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Bunk off work with a mate called Alec and pretend to be ill.
explanation.walkthrough: SKIVE and ALEC are rearranged ('off'). Skive is British slang for dodging work.
explanation.definitionFit: Time away from work while unwell, which a shirker might falsely claim when skipping a day.

clue.text: Washed up silver 11 coin

parts.note: ash, as in ash-blonde, is a pale silvery grey
11 Across is NORSE; the öre is a small Norwegian coin

explanation.surface: A silver Norwegian coin found on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: The 11 refers to the answer at 11 Across, NORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything washed up by the sea has been carried onto the beach, on dry land.

clue.text: German shepherd posed being embraced by a pin-up

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside, so the posing word goes within the others
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a nail is a kind of pin
an artist's model sat, or posed

explanation.surface: A German shepherd dog posing for a pin-up picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pin-up' looks like one word for a glamour poster, but it splits: 'up' turns the pin round, giving LIAN, and 'being embraced by' sets the posing word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsatian is the British name for the German shepherd dog breed.

clue.text: Berlin chap takes in Buddhist temple, it's heaven-sent!

indicators.note: takes in means holds inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: Rainer is a common German man's name
a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia

explanation.surface: A German man visits a Buddhist temple and calls it a godsend.
explanation.definitionFit: Water falling from the sky is literally sent from the heavens, a playful reading of a phrase meaning providential.

clue.text: Mr Klein drops in, sending back soda for something stronger

indicators.note: drops means leaves out the word that follows

parts.note: Calvin Klein is the American fashion designer

indicators.note: sending back means the mixer's letters are reversed

explanation.surface: A fashion designer drops in and refuses a soda, wanting a stiffer drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops in' looks like 'visits'; in fact IN is dropped from CALVIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvados is a Normandy apple brandy, a spirit much stronger than a soft drink.

clue.text: RAF turns up in limitless number circling Cheshire factory

indicators.note: in places the air force letters within the other piece
circling means going round, so the word for a vast number is read backwards

parts.note: a myriad is a countless or unlimited number

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the letters run backwards, bottom to top

explanation.surface: Air force planes appearing in great numbers above a Cheshire works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns up' gives FAR and 'circling' reads the vast number backwards as DAIRYM; 'in' then sets the first inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheshire is also a cheese, so the place that produces it is playfully called a factory for it.

clue.text: 11 involved with wicked CIA plot

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled and wicked suggests twisted, both telling us the letters are mixed up

parts.note: 11 Across is NORSE

explanation.surface: Norwegians mixed up in a sinister CIA conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: NORSE, from 11 Across, and CIA are rearranged ('involved with wicked').
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline of how events may unfold, as in a film's storyline or plot.

clue.text: Corner section of theatrical scenery

definitions.meaning: in football, a corner kick is a rehearsed dead-ball move
a freestanding piece of stage scenery

explanation.surface: A corner of the stage set.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport it is a planned move from a dead ball, such as a corner; on stage, a standalone piece of scenery.

clue.text: Caught sight of Elvis's fringes, of various colours

indicators.note: the fringes of a word are its outermost letters

parts.note: pied means patchily coloured, like a magpie

explanation.surface: Someone glimpsed Elvis's multicoloured fringed costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fringes' suggests the tassels on Elvis's stage suits; it picks the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch a glimpse of something, so espied means spotted or caught sight of.

clue.text: Look about for vacant minicab in Indonesian island

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first word surrounds the other piece
vacant means emptied, keeping only the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: Searching for an empty taxi on an Indonesian island.
explanation.walkthrough: A vacant cab is a free one, but 'vacant' empties 'minicab' to its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lombok is the island east of Bali in Indonesia's Lesser Sunda chain.

clue.text: In adulthood now, Keats rejected combat

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the run is read backwards
in means the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: The grown-up poet Keats turned his back on fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A Korean martial art of kicks and punches, a form of unarmed fighting.

clue.text: Scratch top of fireside clay

indicators.note: to scratch is to strike out, here the top, first letter of the word

parts.note: the hearth is the floor at the fireside

explanation.surface: Scraping the clay off the top of a hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth and clay are both soil, the material of the ground; clay is a kind of earth.

clue.text: He's taking bets for both sides about a "yes" vote

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the two sides wrap round the vote

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, both sides
aye is a yes vote, as in Parliament

explanation.surface: A bookmaker covering both outcomes of a referendum.
explanation.walkthrough: A layer is a bookmaker who 'lays' or accepts bets.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, to lay odds is to accept a wager, so one who does so is a bookmaker.

clue.text: An opponent of Spock's stripped-down language

indicators.note: stripped down means the ends are removed, leaving the inner letters

parts.note: Klingons are the warrior race opposing the Federation in Star Trek, Spock's show

explanation.surface: A Star Trek enemy speaking a pared-back tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Klingon is also a constructed language, a neat red herring for 'language'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for a language, especially foreign speech or jargon.

clue.text: Foul smells left opening of Scotsman's trousers

indicators.note: left means abandoned, so the opening letter of the word is gone

parts.note: breeks is the Scottish word for trousers or breeches

explanation.surface: Bad odours from a Scotsman's trousers left open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a direction or opening on the left; it means departed.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeks are strong unpleasant odours, so the plural noun means stinks or foul smells.

clue.text: A daughter of Mnemosyne, right one to provide inspiration!

parts.note: Erato, muse of love poetry, was one of the nine daughters of Mnemosyne

explanation.surface: A muse, daughter of the goddess of memory, being the right one to inspire.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspiration also means breathing in, so the definition is a device that puts air in.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiration literally means drawing in air, which a device for aerating a lawn or a liquid supplies.

clue.text: Slavery of the debt era?

parts.note: a bond is a certificate of debt
an age is an era

explanation.surface: Asking whether debt is the new form of servitude in our time.
explanation.definitionFit: Bondage is the state of being bound to a master, servitude or enslavement.

clue.text: Head of History in Merkel's school developed an enquiring mind

indicators.note: developed means grown into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A history head teacher at Angela Merkel's school had an inquisitive mind.
explanation.walkthrough: H (head of 'History') goes among MERKELSSCHOOL and all the letters are rearranged ('developed').
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's detective is the archetype of the inquiring intellect, a byword for deductive curiosity.
